hsbc.citi_angle: HSBC's Asian wealth metals franchise is vertically integrated but product-thin outside Hong Kong: the only scaled products are two HK book-entry items (Wayfoong Statement Gold, ~4% max spread, and the SFC-authorised HSBC Gold Token, >US$1bn traded, 2%/5% margin, vaulted in London not Hong Kong), a counter-only Malaysian gold account, HSBC China's gold-linked structured deposits (GLD/GDX and gold-miner baskets, Jan-2026) and the custodian/dealer seat on the new Hang Seng Gold ETF (3170, HK$1.3bn). There is no physical bullion sale, no gold-linked deposit in HK/SG, nothing in Singapore, Taiwan, India (HSBC also lost/never held a 2026-29 bullion-import licence) or Australia, and no published PB precious-metals brochure or metal-collateral Lombard terms. Citi Wealth Asia is behind on the digital/paper-gold rail (no SFC-authorised token, no house paper-gold account with WSG's distribution) but can out-position HSBC where the desk has product: (1) allocated loco-London and loco-Hong Kong/Singapore physical custody for GPB/Premier-Elite-equivalent clients with delivery optionality (HSBC's token and WSG both bar delivery); (2) PM margin loans / share-backed lending against bullion, gold ETFs (2840/3170/GLD) and gold-miner equity - HSBC's Lombard shelf does not publish metal collateral; (3) gold-linked structured deposits and dual-currency-style XAU products for HK/SG affluent clients, matching what HSBC China sells but HSBC HK/SG do not; (4) OTC gold options, accumulators and zero-cost collars for UHNW; (5) a Singapore-booked gold account/physical offer where HSBC SG has nothing, timed with MAS loco-Singapore vaulting (Oct-2026). The 62% of Asia/Middle East affluent investors intending to add gold in 2026 (HSBC's own survey) is demand HSBC's non-HK entities cannot currently serve with a proprietary product.

anz.citi_angle: ANZ is a liquidity competitor, not a wealth-shelf competitor: its only client-facing metals product is the A$128m State Street Gold Fund feeder into GLDM that ANZ Private commissioned in 2024 (0.14% fee, no physical, no Lombard, no structured notes), while retail broking, Asian wealth and physical custody have all been divested (CMC 2023, DBS 2018, Singapore vault closed 2019). Three angles for Citi. (1) ANZ Private white-space: with a ~A$9bn book running an explicit gold overweight, ANZ Private has no allocated-metal, delivery, gold-collateral lending or gold-linked note capability - Citi can offer ANZ Private/its DIMS (or the ex-ANZ HNW clients now at CMC/DBS) allocated loco-London gold, gold-backed Lombard lines and AUD gold-linked structured notes that the SSGA fund cannot. (2) Institutional: ANZ's commodity trading assets jumped to A$9.1bn and commodity VaR nearly tripled in FY25 - the desk is rebuilding physical/consignment inventory for Asian refiner-jeweller flows using its PBoC import licence, SGE fixing seat and CFETS market-making status; ANZ is an LBMA full member (not a market maker) and now lacks its own vault, so it needs loco-London/Zurich liquidity, leasing, swaps and custody from market makers - Citi (LPMCL member since Jul-2026) should be a counterparty of choice for ANZ's Asia book (location swaps London<>Shanghai/Singapore, consignment funding, Pt/Pd options which ANZ only offers via its FX options desk). (3) Product intel: the State Street/GLDM feeder shows Australian private banks will outsource gold to a US ETF rather than build accounts - a Citi-custodied AUD unallocated/allocated account or feeder with delivery optionality priced near 0.14% would be a direct displacement pitch to ANZ Private, NAB/CBA/Westpac private and Australian IFAs.

standard.citi_angle: SCB's wealth gold shelf is thin relative to its bullion-desk footprint: the only explicit metal balance for wealth clients is an unallocated line in Jersey, there is no gold account in SG/HK/MY/KR/TW, no physical/allocated custody for PB clients (physical gold, options financing and the planned HK vault are CIB-only), Singapore PCI excludes XAU, and India has lost its import licence for 2026-29. Gold reaches SCB wealth clients through the CIO 7% allocation, gold ETFs, gold-linked structured notes and the new AllianzGI-managed Enhanced Gold Income Fund (gold ETFs + covered calls). For Citi: (1) the Enhanced Gold Income Fund and SCB PB structured-note desk need cheap gold-ETF/XAU option liquidity - Citi (full LBMA market maker incl. forwards; SCB quotes only spot+options) can be a forwards/vol provider to SCB's structuring desk; (2) SCB is now a $25bn precious-metals balance-sheet holder (from $5.6bn) with rising commodity VaR - a natural counterparty for balance-sheet relief via metal repo/lease and for loco-London <-> loco-HK swaps as HKPMCC scales; (3) SCB PB clients wanting allocated physical, PM-margin loans or loco-Singapore/HK physical have no in-house product - Citi PB/markets can position allocated custody and share-/bullion-backed lending against that gap; (4) SCB is custodian/trustee for LionGlobal Physical Gold (SG) and ChinaAMC Digital Gold ETF (HK), so the ETF-custody battleground in Asia is SCB vs JPM/HSBC/ICBC - Citi should pitch on the next HK/SG physical/tokenised gold ETF mandate before SCB's HK vault is built.

firms.shelf_summary: In-house bullion liquidity, not a client-wealth shelf. ANZ is an LBMA FULL member (NOT one of the 12 LBMA Market Makers - correct the premise), a Shanghai Gold Benchmark fixing bank (1 of 12), SGEI international member, PBoC-licensed gold importer via ANZ Shanghai (Dec-2013), and a CFETS interbank gold first-tier market maker (2016). Historically one of Asia's largest bullion businesses (c.15% of world primary gold production distributed in 2013; Perth Mint overseas-distribution agreement not renewed in 2016; Risk 'Asia metals dealer of the year' 2015 and Energy Risk Asia Precious Metals House of the Year under Eddie Listorti). Scaled back 2018-19 (sold physical-gold ETF JV stake 2018; closed Singapore vault Jan-2019) but FY25 shows a re-expansion: commodities trading assets A$9.08bn (+42% yoy), commodity derivative fair values doubled, commodities VaR A$8.9m as at 30-Sep-2025 vs A$3.3m. Institutional product page: swaps and options in gold, silver, platinum, palladium (options via FX Options desk) plus inventory finance, flow hedging and structured/bundled commodity finance. The '2016 precious-metals spot-fixing settlement' in the brief could NOT be verified - ANZ's 2016-17 ASIC settlement was BBSW (A$50m, Nov-2017), not metals.
